gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Apex 300's built-in solar inputs take only 12–60 V DC (2 × 1,200 W, 20 A), while its SolarX 4K add-on controller needs a 150–500 V panel string. A string between 60 V and 150 V fits neither, so the panel wiring decides whether the $699 SolarX 4K has to be in the cart.
standout_why: I compared this against watthourlab.com/home-backup/transfer-switch-basics (cited) and outagereadyhq.com/best/best-whole-home-battery-backup (rank 1). Watthourlab gives only total solar watts (DELTA Pro 3 at 2,600 W, F3800 Plus at 3,200 W) and nothing on voltage windows. OutageReadyHQ says outright that it gives 'no series wiring or Voc guidance' and does not cover 240 V output while charging. I could not open the Popular Mechanics page (cited; the fetch was blocked), solargenreview.com (HTTP 429) or energysavvyhomes.com (certificate error), so I can't rule out that one of them has it. Both pages I read list the Apex 300 Home Backup Kit ($3,399 regular, per OutageReadyHQ) and the F3800 Plus transfer-switch bundles. Neither says which solar hardware a home-scale panel string needs, and that is the part that changes what goes in the cart.
kit_items: Battery/inverter: BLUETTI Apex 300 (2,764.8 Wh, 3,840 W). StorageReview found that one unit makes 240 V by itself: it has two inverters, one per line, and the NEMA 14-50R gives 120/240 V in 240 V mode. That means a second unit is not needed just to run 240 V loads.
Expansion battery: BLUETTI B300K. Apex 300 + B300K comes to 5,529.6 Wh. StorageReview measured 7.38 kWh delivered from the stack with two B300K.
Home connection: BLUETTI Apex 300 Home Integration Kit (Single Apex 300). It is the maker's own panel or switch for feeding home circuits. The listing does not state its circuit count or amp rating.

Solar charge controller: BLUETTI SolarX 4K. It takes a 150–500 V string, steps it down below 60 V, and adds up to 4 kW. A roof-style series string goes over the Apex 300's own 60 V input limit, so you need this controller for one.

Panels: BLUETTI SORA 500 (500 W, MC4) or 200 W foldables. On the built-in input they must be wired so each input stays at or below 60 V Voc, which in practice means single or parallel panels. To use the SolarX 4K, they must be wired in series to reach 150 V or more.
Installation: a licensed electrician. Watthourlab and OutageReadyHQ both say this, and OutageReadyHQ lists installation as 'Not included' for the BLUETTI kit.

findings.label: 240 V from a single unit

findings.label: Grid input limit on a 240 V supply in 120 V mode
findings.value: The limit applies to one leg only. The unit draws from one line until the output is switched to 240 V mode.
findings.note: The limit can be set from 1 to 50 A in 1 A steps in the app.
